sources.title: Passport for Travel to North Korea
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Passport Services
sources.jurisdiction: United States / Democratic People's Republic of Korea
sources.officialityEvidence: The live U.S. Passport Services page, updated 20 March 2026, directly defines the validity of ordinary U.S. passports for DPRK travel and limits special validation to national-interest exceptions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: U.S. passports are not valid for travel to, in, or through North Korea.

sources.title: North Korea travel advice and advisories
sources.jurisdiction: Canada / Democratic People's Republic of Korea
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Government of Canada page, updated 29 July 2026, separates regular Canadian passports from official and other documents, then identifies the required tourist visa and its third-country DPRK-mission route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Canadians must have a visa to enter North Korea.

sources.title: North Korea Travel Advice & Safety
sources.publisher: Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
sources.jurisdiction: Australia / Democratic People's Republic of Korea
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Smartraveller page, updated 31 March 2026, directly tells Australian travellers that every travel type needs a DPRK visa and identifies advance acquisition in a third country.
sources.supportingExcerpt: If, despite our advice, you travel to North Korea, you need a visa for all types of travel.

policies.title: Ordinary U.S. passports: North Korea travel restriction
policies.summary: U.S. Passport Services states that ordinary U.S. passports are invalid for travel to, in or through North Korea. A separately issued special-validation passport is limited to national-interest cases and is not an ordinary short-tourist route.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary U.S. passport for travel to, in or through North Korea.
Passport Services may issue a special-validation passport only on a limited national-interest basis, including qualifying journalism, Red Cross work or compelling humanitarian cases.
A special validation is a separate passport exception and does not itself decide DPRK admission or replace any DPRK entry permission.

policies.title: Regular Canadian passports: North Korea advance visa
policies.summary: Canada's current regular-passport guidance requires a tourist visa and says it is obtained before travel from a DPRK mission in a third country after approval from Pyongyang.
conditions: Applies to a regular Canadian passport; official and other travel documents may follow different rules.
The visa is obtained from a North Korean mission in a third country after approval from the government in Pyongyang, and the process may be slow.
The passport must remain valid for at least six months beyond expected departure; journalists need special permission and may not use a tourist visa.
Border operations, organized-tour requirements, carrier rules and final admission remain separate and can change.

policies.title: Australian passports: North Korea advance visa
policies.summary: Australia's current travel guidance requires a visa for every travel type and directs applicants to obtain it in a third country because no DPRK mission operates in Australia.
conditions: Applies to Australian travellers using an ordinary passport for a short visit; journalists and business travellers follow additional permission or sponsorship rules.
The visa must be obtained before travel in a third country such as China or Indonesia because there is no DPRK embassy or consulate in Australia.
Travel is limited to an official tour with an accompanying guide; sanctions may also affect payments connected to a visa or organized travel.
Entry conditions, carrier rules and final admission remain separate and may change at short notice.

policies.title: Chinese private ordinary passports: North Korea advance visa
policies.summary: China's current consular guidance requires private ordinary-passport holders to obtain a DPRK visa or tourism certificate outside North Korea before travel through a DPRK mission or authorized tourism channel.
conditions: Applies to a Chinese private ordinary passport; diplomatic, service and public-affairs ordinary passports have a separate treaty route.
A DPRK visa must be handled before travel by a DPRK diplomatic or consular mission outside North Korea; an authorized travel agency handles the alternative tourism certificate.
A DPRK receiving organization or organized-tour channel is required, and in-country movement and registration are controlled.
Transit, border-area permits, other passport types and final admission remain outside this classification.

conflicts.explanation: The fallback treats the ordinary U.S. route as an advance visa, but Passport Services makes the passport itself invalid for DPRK travel unless a limited special validation is separately granted.
